info.title: Translation Hub
info.description: Read-only views of Bible translation work on WACS: repos, books, checks, catalog status.

get.summary: Books BIEL shows twice: two repos both Primary and shown on BIEL.
Every check across every repo, most findings first: where a rule is noisy.
The repos where one check fires most.
Languages that have repos here, most repos first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the code, the names and the alternate names.

get.summary: One language: its facts, its repos, and per book which repo is Official.

A language and brand's Writer books over time: verses per book after each
save, and saves per author per week.

Per resource of a language: what is published (a publisher's choice, or
the official org's repo by default), its newest release, or a suggestion.

post.summary:
Make a repo the published text for a language and resource (a pointer; no
copy is made), or clear the choice. Publishers only.

get.summary:
Every copy of every book of a language and brand, grouped into variants by
their words, with the pick and the official copy's state.

parameters.name: against
parameters.description:
More sources to measure progress against, `owner/name,owner/name`
(a reader's pins), after the ones the copies declare (the three most
declared).

get.summary: Two copies of a book, verse by verse: the verses whose words differ.

parameters.name: a
parameters.description: `owner/name`: the copy shown on the left (usually the published one).

post.summary: Set a copy aside for one book or every book, or bring it back. Publishers only.

200.description: Whether the copy is now set aside

get.summary: Who is signed in.
The signed-in person's languages and projects.
Repos, newest HEAD first: the home feed and search.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches owner/name, title or language code.

parameters.name: synthetic
parameters.description: Only synthetic (Writer) repos, or only real ones.

get.summary:
One repo at HEAD: manifest, books with lint and coverage, catalog rows,
the sous-chef summary.

post.summary: Adopt: fork this consolidated repo into the official org as its language and brand's official repo.

get.summary:
Every Writer candidate per book for this repo's language and brand, the
default pick marked, each with its saves and progress over time (read
from the repos' history, in parallel).

One book beside its source, verse by verse: both texts, both lengths
(graphemes, as Sous Chef counts them), the book's usual ratio, and the
length lane's flags.

parameters.name: chapter
parameters.description: Only this chapter's verses (the usual ratio still covers the book).

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Include the verse texts (default true). Off for charts of the whole book.

get.summary: What the hub saw each time the book changed: lint and coverage over time.
The newest commits on the default branch.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (default 100, at most 500).

post.summary:
Consolidate: every Writer project of this one's language and brand (one per
book) into a NEW official repo, every save that changed a book kept as a
commit (crates/history, ported from Sefer's writerHistory.ts), then the RC
manifest. Built locally and pushed as the service account. Only when the
official repo does not exist: after that, books come in by pull, and a repo
that is already consolidated is adopted instead.

get.summary:
Verses present per chapter, this repo against a source (verse numbers, as
the progress strip counts them).

parameters.name: against
parameters.description:
The source to measure against, `owner/name`. Default: the one this
repo declares, else the one its language's copies declare most.

get.summary:
One file's bytes at HEAD, with a content type from its extension (text as
UTF-8, audio playable in the browser).

parameters.name: source
parameters.description:
For a synthetic repo, read the real Writer file at `path` instead of the
synthetic one.

get.summary:
Every check that fired in the repo (lint and Sous Chef), most findings
first, each with its count per book.
The official repo this one publishes to, its releases, and what the signed-in person may do.
Sous Chef rows from the last run, for one book and/or one check.

post.summary: Pull one book of this repo (a Writer project's stitched book) into the official repo, as one commit.
Publish: a release tag at the head of this official repo (or of this repo's official one).

get.summary:
A markdown or TSV file as sanitised HTML, links rewritten to the hub's
pages (relative paths, `rc://` resource links) or kept (web links).
Whether the signed-in person starred this repo on Forgejo.

post.summary: Star or unstar this repo on Forgejo, as the signed-in person.

get.summary: The repo's files at HEAD. A Writer repo answers with its synthetic files.
What changed since the newest release tag: commits, and each book in verses.
Totals and watermarks: how much is indexed and how fresh it is.

Assembly.description: What a consolidation would gather, book by book, before it runs.

target.description: The official repo it would create: `TextTranslation/twx_reg`.

BielConflict.description:
A book BIEL shows twice: two repos both Primary and shown, for one
language, domain, resource type and track (workTracker's rule).

oneOf.description: Absent: the book is new since the release.

diff.description: The book now against the book at the release.

path.description: This repo's file for the book; absent when the repo lacks it.

source.description: The source the run compared against, `owner/name@sha` as recorded.

source_path.description: The source file read (at the source's current HEAD).

BookCopy.description:
One copy of a book in a language and brand: a Writer project, a
consolidated repo, or the official one.

findings.description: Proofreading findings in this book at the last run.

path.description: The file in the repo (the stitched file for a Writer project).

source_repo.description: The source the repo declares for this book, `owner/name`.

BookCount.description: One check's count in one book.

BookCoverage.description:
One book's verses against a source: how many of the source's verses the
book has (by number), of how many.

verses.description: Verses that differ, in order (at most 2,000).

BookPick.description:
One book of one version (resource type + track) in a language, with the
repos that could be its text and the rules' verdicts on them.

shown_twice_on_biel.description: BIEL stitches two sources for this book (both Primary and shown).

points.description: `[unix seconds, verses present]` after each save that changed the count.

repo.description: The Writer project it was read from, `owner/name`.

source_verses.description: The source's verse count, when a source resolves: the book's target.

BookRow.description: One book of a repo at HEAD.

default.description: The default pick: Primary and shown on BIEL first (`default_pick`).

progress.description:
Verses present at 30 evenly spaced times from the first save to the
last: the book's progress toward its full count.

saves.description: Writer saves that changed the book's text.

Candidate.description: One candidate for a book, with what helps pick it.

CatalogRef.description: A catalog row that points at this repo.

present.description: The source's verses this chapter has (by number).

total.description: The source's verses in the chapter.

CodeCount.description: One check across a repo: its total and its books, most first.

by.description: Who asked the hub for it: `Pulled-by:` or `Consolidated-by:`.

source.description: Where the change came from: `Source:` (a pull) or `Writer-Source:` (a replayed save).

flag.description: The length lane's verdict on this verse, when it fired: `Long` or `Short`.

picks.description:
Per book (`MRK`), the Writer project to take (`owner/name`), or `""` to
leave the book out. A book not named gets the default pick.

ignored.description: Set aside by a publisher, for this book or for every book.

Coverage.description: A repo against a source, chapter by chapter, in the source's book order.

candidates.description: Sources one could pick instead: declared by the repo or its language's copies.

source.description: `owner/name` measured against; absent when none could be found.

extra.description: Verses the source does not have; usually versification, not an error.

gaps.description: Chapter → missing verse numbers; only chapters with gaps.

Diff.description: How one copy differs from another, in verses.

added.description: Verses this one has and the other lacks.

changed.description: Verses in both, with different words.

missing.description: Verses the other has and this one lacks.

html_url.description: Forgejo's page for what was written.

message.description: What was written, in a sentence.

Evidence.description:
The fraction behind one convention finding. Every site of one pattern
carries the same evidence; `pattern` says which sites belong together.

books.description:
Books holding part of the numerator (saturates at 255), out of
`Proof::books.len()`.

denominator.description: …out of how many chances (the comparison population).

pattern.description:
The pattern's row in this corpus's table; stable only within one
[`Proof`].

oneOf.description: What the corpus usually does instead, when the pattern names it.

Finding.description:
One reviewable site.

**Offsets are UTF-16 code units into the raw book text** (`from..to`,
half-open), which is what CodeMirror positions are. A site whose content
crosses removed markup (a footnote, a marker) gets the BOUNDING raw range:
first content character through last.

chapter.description: 0 for front matter, before the first `\c`.

code.description:
Sous's own name for what fired: a hygiene class (`StrayCarriageReturn`)
or the pattern's channel (`Rarity`, `Casing`, …).

oneOf.description: Convention: the counts behind the claim.

id.description: The host id of the book ([`Book::id`]).

message.description:
One plain English sentence. The claim is narrow on purpose: rare, not
wrong.

oneOf.description: Source-compared lanes: what the comparison with the source found.

reasons.description:
Every way a convention site is unusual, Sous's `Reasons` names; the
`code` is the finest of them. Empty for hygiene.

rule.description:
The lane: `hygiene` (deterministic: the text should never hold this)
or `convention` (corpus-relative: this corpus rarely does this).

run.description: Hygiene: how many offending characters are in the run.

HistoryPoint.description: One point of a book's history: what the hub saw when it changed.

mine.description: Repos the person or one of their organisations owns, newest first.

starred.description: Repos starred on WACS, in Forgejo's order.

repos.description: Repos where it fires at least once.

top_repo_share.description:
Share of the total in the single noisiest repo, 0–1: near 1 means one
repo (often one script's convention) explains the count.

book.description: A USFM id, or `*` for every book the repo holds.

books.description: From the catalog: per version and book, which repo is Official.

LanguageResource.description: One resource (brand) of a language: how many repos, how many of them Writer projects.

official.description: Repos in `org` (the official org) for this language and resource.

repos.description: Scanned public repos whose manifest names this language.

languages.description: IETF tags, in the order to show them.

moved.description: It has commits since the pull.

repo.description: The repo the published book was pulled from (it tracks), `owner/name`.

version.description: Its variant now, when it still has the book.

by_chapter.description: Chapter → `[errors, warnings, infos]`; chapter 0 is before the first `\c`.

ManifestInfo.description: The manifest as the scan read it.

error.description: Why the manifest did not parse, when it did not.

Me.description: A signed-in person, as the API shows them.

publisher.description: In the official org's publishers team at sign-in.

official_org.description: The official org (`TextTranslation`), when publishing is on.

publishing.description: Whether this hub can sign people in and publish at all.

Official.description: What the official side looks like from one repo's page.

actions.description: What the hub wrote from this repo, or to it.

can_adopt.description: Adopt is offered: a consolidated (not Writer) repo, and no official repo yet.

can_publish.description: The signed-in person may adopt, pull and publish.

is_official.description: This repo is itself in the official org.

oneOf.description:
Where this repo's language and brand publish: `{org}/{ietf}_{resource}`.
Null when the repo declares no language or resource.

writer_books.description:
Consolidate is offered (a Writer project, no official repo yet): the
language and brand's Writer books it would gather, one per book.

exists.description: Whether it exists on Forgejo yet.

PairedEvidence.description:
The facts behind one source-compared finding (`rule: "source"`). Source
copy's run of shared words is [`Finding::run`].

eligible.description: Source copy: target words in the verse that could be compared.

keys.description:
Presence: consecutive verse keys the row covers, a bridge counting once.
`chapter`/`verse` are the first of them.

kind.description:
`LengthProportionality`: `Long` or `Short`. `Presence`: `Missing` (the
source has verses the book lacks; the span is where they would go),
`Extra` (the book has verses the source lacks) or `Empty` (the verse
is there but holds nothing). `SourceCopy`: `Copy`.

target_len.description: Length: graphemes in the target verse and in its source verse.

z_book.description:
Length: how many spreads this verse's target/source ratio sits from the
usual ratio in this book, and in the whole repo. `None` when that scope
had too few paired verses to judge (sous's `min_verses`, 50).

book.description: The `\id` code as written, first three bytes: `MAT`.

source.description:
The source book this one was compared with ([`proofread_paired`]),
by its host id; `None` when there was no source or it lacks this book.

ProofCorpus.description:
The run's corpus: which books formed it and which were left out. Stored
as the proof's summary body.

source.description:
The source text the run compared against, `owner/name@sha`; absent
when the repo resolves none.

source_copy.description: Whether the source-copy lane ran (only when the languages differ).

ProofPage.description: Documentation only: the shape `repo_proof` assembles from stored JSON.

corpus.description: Which books formed the corpus, and which were left out.

findings.description:
The stored rows that match, in book order. At most
`ROWS_PER_BOOK_CODE` (200) per book and check are stored; the true
counts are in `/findings`.

current.description: False when HEAD moved since the run; a new run is queued.

repo.description: `owner/name` to make the published text, or null to clear the choice.

Published.description: What is published for one resource of a language, or what could be.

last_tag.description: Its newest release tag, and when.

repos.description: Repos of this language and resource.

suggest.description:
With nothing published: the repo to bless first (WA-Catalog's, else
the one with the most books), when there is a consolidated one.

PublishedBook.description: The published copy of one book, and what it tracks.

state.description:
`current` (same words as the repo it tracks), `behind` (that repo
changed since), `edited` (the published copy changed, the repo did not),
`unlinked` (no record of where it came from).

oneOf.description: The tracked repo's copy against the published one, when they differ.

PublishedRef.description: What is published for this language and resource.

chosen.description: A publisher chose it; false: the official org's `{ietf}_{resource}` by default.

writable.description: In the official org, so the hub may pull into it and release from it.

Release.description: A release, as the hub shows it.

bulletins.description:
The bulletin in other languages. With any, every version (`notes`
too) is committed as `bulletins/{tag}/{language}.md` just before the
tag, so the translations travel with the text they describe.

notes.description: The bulletin: what changed, for readers. The release's own text.

html.description: Sanitised HTML, safe to put in the page as is.

truncated.description: A TSV longer than the rows shown.

RepoCodeCount.description: One repo's count for one check.

allOf.description: The same fields the lists show, at the top level.

oneOf.description: Set when the repo is a Writer project served as a synthetic repo.

RepoSummary.description: One repo in a list: the feed, search, a language page.

head_unix.description: Committer time of HEAD, Unix seconds.

is_synthetic.description: Served as a synthetic repo (a Writer project stitched into one book).

status.description: The catalog's label, when the public data API lists this repo.

synthetic.description:
True for a Writer repo: `files` is the synthetic repo the hub serves
(it is not a real repo), and `source_files` the Writer chunks it was
stitched from.

pick.description:
The variant the hub would take: the one the published copy tracks,
else the best variant not set aside.

reference.description:
What the other variants are compared with: the published copy's
variant, else the pick.

source_verses.description: Verses in the gateway source, when one resolves.

SourceProgress.description:
The language and brand's text (the official copy, else the pick) against
one source, book by book in the source's order.

progress.description: Against each source asked for (or declared).

target.description: `TextTranslation/{ietf}_{resource}`, where the hub would create one, when publishing is configured.

Star.description:
Whether the signed-in person starred a repo: Forgejo's own pin, which is
how the hub's Your work follows a repo.

SyntheticInfo.description: What the hub serves in place of a Writer repo's chunk files.

chapters.description: Chapters that have at least one chunk.

chunk_files.description: How many Writer files it was stitched from.

state.description: Watermarks: last poll, last catalog fetch, and so on (Unix seconds).

TreeEntry.description: One file or directory in a repo's tree.

books.description: USFM files whose verses changed since it.

last_tag.description: The newest release tag behind HEAD; absent before the first release.

text.description: A mark in brackets (`[']`), a word form, or a class (`a letter`).

Variant.description:
A variant: copies with the same words in every verse. (A *version* is a
release, `v1.0`; a variant is just a distinct text.)

members.description:
Best first: Primary and on BIEL, then Primary, Active, unlisted; then
the most verses, the newest. The published copy is not listed here:
it is the book's `published`, what the others are compared with.

published.description: The published copy has these words.

oneOf.description: Against the reference (the published copy, else the pick); absent for the reference itself.

VerseChange.description: One verse that differs between two copies; a side is absent when that copy lacks the verse.

VersePair.description: One target verse beside its source.

last.description: The last verse of a bridge (`1-2` → 2); equal to `verse` otherwise.

target.description:
The verse text (onion's projection: markers and notes removed, spaces
collapsed); empty when the caller asked for lengths only.

WeekSaves.description: Saves by one author in one week.

week.description: Start of the week, unix seconds (weeks from the epoch, a Thursday).

WriterBook.description: One book of a Writer project, a candidate for consolidation.

source_verses.description: Against the declared source, when one resolves.

status.description: The catalog's status for this repo (`Primary`, `Active`, `Inactive`), when listed.
